The Loops page is a project-level view inside Invent that organizes all loops running in your project — monitors watching for problems, recurring routines Invent runs on your behalf, and loops grouped by the agent or workforce they belong to.

<div className="invent-callout">
  <strong>Invent can set this up for you.</strong> Ask Invent to create a routine with a name and a purpose, and it writes the standing instructions, sets the cadence, and starts running it on schedule.
</div>

## How to access the Loops page

Open Invent, then click **Loops** in the left navigation panel of your project.

## The three sections

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Performance loops" icon="bell">
    Alarms that monitor agents and workforces for problems. These run diagnostics and alert you when something needs attention.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Scheduled loops" icon="calendar-clock">
    Recurring Invent routines that run on a daily or weekly cadence. Invent carries out the work autonomously on your behalf.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Asset loops" icon="layer-group">
    Loops grouped by the agent or workforce they are associated with. Use this view to see all loops for a specific asset.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Scheduled loops (routines)

A scheduled loop is a recurring routine where Invent works on your project on a set cadence — daily or weekly. You write standing instructions once; Invent runs them on schedule without any manual input.

<Note>
  Scheduled loops are not agent triggers. Agent triggers start an individual agent on a schedule. A scheduled loop is Invent itself working autonomously on your behalf — reading task history, updating memories, reviewing prompts, and proposing improvements.
</Note>

### Creating a routine from a template

The **Scheduled loops** section includes an **Add new** button with a dropdown of six pre-built routine templates. Each template pre-fills the name, standing instructions, and default cadence so you can get started without writing instructions from scratch.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Loops page">
    In Invent, click **Loops** in the left navigation panel.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open the Add new dropdown">
    In the **Scheduled loops** section, click the arrow on the **Add new** button to expand the dropdown.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select a template">
    Choose one of the six templates from the dropdown. The routine opens pre-filled with a name, standing instructions, and a default cadence.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Review and save">
    Adjust the name, instructions, or cadence if needed, then save the routine.
  </Step>
</Steps>

#### Available templates

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Reflect (daily)">
    Reads yesterday's agent tasks and looks for patterns — repeated errors, slow steps, or missed instructions — then summarizes what needs fixing. Runs daily.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Dream (daily)">
    Turns what Invent learns about your goals and working patterns into lasting memories, so it can act with better context over time. Runs daily.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Grow evals (daily)">
    Converts real agent tasks into evaluation cases that catch regressions before they reach production. Runs daily.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Sharpen instructions (weekly)">
    Compares each agent's prompt against how it actually behaves in live tasks, then proposes prompt improvements where behavior and instructions diverge. Runs weekly.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Cost optimize (daily)">
    Identifies which agents and tools are consuming the most credits and suggests where usage can be reduced. Runs daily.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Grow use cases (weekly)">
    Finds recurring work in your project that has no agent handling it yet, and proposes a new agent or workflow for each gap. Runs weekly.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### Creating a routine from scratch

To create a custom routine without using a template:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Loops page">
    In Invent, click **Loops** in the left navigation panel.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Click Add new">
    In the **Scheduled loops** section, click **Add new** (not the dropdown arrow).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Write standing instructions">
    Give the routine a name and write the standing instructions — what Invent should do each time this routine runs.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Set the cadence">
    Choose daily or weekly, then set the time or day the routine should run.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save">
    Save the routine. It will run automatically on the schedule you set.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Managing routines

### Editing a routine

Open the Loops page, find the routine in the **Scheduled loops** section, and click on it to open the editor. Update the name, standing instructions, or cadence, then save your changes.

### Deleting a routine

Open the routine from the **Scheduled loops** section, then use the delete option in the routine editor. Deleting a routine is permanent and cannot be undone.

## Frequently asked questions

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="What is the difference between a scheduled loop and a scheduled agent trigger?">
    A scheduled agent trigger starts a specific agent on a timer — the agent then runs its task as normal. A scheduled loop is Invent itself working on your project on a recurring basis, reading history, updating context, and proposing improvements. They serve different purposes and are configured in different places.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I run a scheduled loop immediately instead of waiting for the next scheduled time?">
    Open the routine from the Scheduled loops section and use the run option to trigger it manually outside its normal cadence.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How do I see what a scheduled loop did when it ran?">
    Each loop run appears in Invent's task history. Open Invent and look at the conversation history to find the routine's output from each run.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Can I have more than one routine of the same template type?">
    Yes. You can create multiple routines from the same template or from scratch. Each runs independently on its own schedule.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
